title: Calling super() and this() from constructors
answer: A constructor cannot explicitly invoke both `this(...)` and `super(...)` directly because an explicit constructor invocation must be the first statement, and only one such invocation can occupy that position. A constructor may call `this(...)`, and the target constructor can then call `super(...)`, producing an indirect chain. If neither is written where required, Java inserts an implicit `super()` when a compatible no-arg superclass constructor exists.
